prompt.context: Our client is Caesars, one of the largest gaming and resort companies in the world. Penn and Teller have been the headlining show at the Rio Hotel since 2001, and they are currently the longest-running headlining show in Vegas history. Caesars, who owns the Rio Hotel where the duo performs in the 1500 seat P&T Theater, is wondering if their act has become stale. Penn & Teller's annual contract is about to expire, and before Caesars has a meeting with the duo they have asked our company's advice on whether or not to resign the act for another year.
prompt.question: What recommendation do you have for Caesars?

clarifying_info.a: As one of the largest entertainment companies on the Strip and around the world, Caesars solely cares about the company's total bottom line profitability.

clarifying_info.q: How long is a contract for Penn & Teller?
clarifying_info.a: As is the Vegas standard, all contracts are for a one-year time period.

clarifying_info.q: Why does Caesars think the show is stale?
clarifying_info.a: The show has plateaued, with no change in bottom line profitability in the past five years.
Caesars's biggest competitor is MGM Resorts, which also operates about 33% of the Strip. P&T compete against a whole bevy of nighttime entertainment, such as other shows, nightclubs, and gaming.

exhibits.title: Revenue per Show — Seat Categories
exhibits.shows: A table listing the three seat categories (A, B, C) with number of seats and ticket price for each category; a separate panel shows revenue scaling from per-show to annual.
exhibits.data: Category A: 300 seats, $120; Category B: 800 seats, $75; Category C: 400 seats, $55; 6 shows/week, 40 weeks/year

exhibits.title: Revenue Calculation Filled
exhibits.shows: A completed revenue table showing attendance per show, ticket revenue per show by category, total revenue per show, and annualized revenue.
exhibits.data: Cat A: 300 seats sold, $36,000/show; Cat B: 640 seats sold, $48,000/show; Cat C: 200 seats sold, $11,000/show; Revenue per show: $95,000; Annual revenue: $22.8M

exhibits.title: Cost Items — Inputs
exhibits.shows: A list of cost line items with the cost rate and time period (per show, per week, per month, per year) but without the annualized totals filled in.
exhibits.data: Performer contracts: $2M per person/year; Crew: $2,000/show; Housekeeping: $1,000/week (40 weeks only); Props: $200/show; Utilities: $52,000/year; SG&A/Marketing: $15,000/month (12 months)

exhibits.title: Cost Calculation Filled
exhibits.shows: A completed cost table with annualized cost for each item and a total annual cost figure.
exhibits.data: Performer contracts: $4,000,000; Crew: $480,000; Housekeeping: $40,000; Props: $48,000; Utilities: $52,000; SG&A/MKTG: $180,000; Total cost/year: $4,800,000

exhibits.title: Profit Summary
exhibits.shows: A summary showing annual revenue, annual costs, annual profit, and margin.

framework: Profits from P&T: Revenue (ticket pricing x seats x occupancy x shows) vs. Costs (fixed: contracts, SG&A, utilities; variable: crew, props, housekeeping)
Revenues — Ticket Costs: pricing tiers (A/B/C), % seats sold per tier, shows per week, weeks per year
Costs — Fixed: performer annual contracts, marketing/SG&A, insurance; Variable: magic props, housekeeping, ushers/stage crew, utilities
Other sources of company profit beyond P&T show: incremental hotel stays, dining, casino/gaming spend, drinks, souvenirs, concessions
Framework should go three levels deep, use case-specific terminology (seats/patrons not units/customers), be MECE, and consider total company bottom line

questions.prompt: How much annual revenue does the Penn & Teller show generate?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a per-show revenue model by seat category, then scale to annual. Strong answers use shortcuts (e.g., approximate $95K/show x 240 shows). Should track units carefully (thousands/millions).

math.setup: Revenue per show = (seats x occupancy x price) summed across A, B, C tiers; Annual = revenue/show x shows/week x weeks/year
steps: Annual shows = 6 shows/week x 40 weeks = 240 shows

questions.prompt: What are the total annual costs of the Penn & Teller show?
questions.guidance: Candidate must convert all costs to a common annual basis. Key pitfall: housekeeping is only 40 weeks (show weeks), SG&A is 12 months. Crew and props are per-show and must be multiplied by 240 shows/year.

math.setup: Annualize each cost item; sum them

questions.prompt: What is the annual profit and margin of the Penn & Teller show?
questions.guidance: Straightforward subtraction. Candidate should note the very high ~80% margin and comment on what that implies for the decision.

math.setup: Annual Profit = Revenue - Costs; Margin = Profit / Revenue

questions.prompt: Caesars has the opportunity to switch the P&T show for one featuring the recent winner of America's Got Talent (AGT). The switch requires a one-time cost of $2.4M (theater reconfiguration + marketing blitz). The AGT show generates $90K in ticket revenue per show and costs $3M per year. Should Caesars make the switch, and what is the payback period?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute the incremental profit change and then divide the one-time cost by annual incremental benefit to get payback period. Should weigh both financial and qualitative factors (market competitiveness, longevity risk of AGT winner).

math.setup: Incremental annual profit = (AGT annual profit) - (P&T annual profit); Payback = one-time cost / incremental annual profit
steps: AGT revenue per show = $90,000 vs P&T $95,000 → delta = -$5,000/show
AGT annual revenue change = -$5,000 x 240 shows = -$1,200,000/year
AGT annual costs = $3,000,000 vs P&T $4,800,000 → cost saving = +$1,800,000/year
math.answer: AGT show is $600K more profitable per year; payback period is 4 years

brainstorming.prompt: What can Caesars do to make the current P&T show more profitable?

categories.name: Revenue — Ticket Pricing
ideas: Convert some Category B seats into Category A (higher margin)
Convert some Category C seats into Category B

categories.name: Revenue — Quantity
ideas: Offer bundle discounts to drive occupancy in low-fill tiers
Partner with hotels to bundle tickets with overnight stays

categories.name: Revenue — Other
ideas: Retool concessions offerings for higher margin
Add a gift shop with P&T-branded souvenirs
Shorten the show to drive more casino floor time (higher-margin activity)
Bundle tickets with dinner packages or other Rio Hotel activities

categories.name: Costs
ideas: Revisit and renegotiate contract terms with Penn & Teller
Review union vs. non-union labor for crew positions
Optimize prop procurement to reduce per-show costs

recommendation: Option A (Resign P&T): The P&T show is highly profitable at $18M annual profit on $22.8M revenue (~80% margin). The AGT switch carries a 4-year payback period in a highly competitive, fast-moving market, making it too risky.

Option B (Switch to AGT): While AGT would generate $600K more annual profit, the 4-year payback is long in Vegas's competitive entertainment landscape, and the AGT winner may lack long-lasting appeal.
Primary recommendation: Resign P&T, as the show's profitability is strong and the alternative carries significant execution and longevity risk.
risks: P&T show has plateaued with no growth for 5+ years — staleness risk is real
AGT winner's appeal could fade quickly in a competitive market
4-year payback period leaves Caesars exposed to competitor moves (MGM controls ~33% of the Strip)
Reconfiguration costs are sunk once committed
next_steps: Explore revenue enhancement opportunities: price optimization, seat-category reallocation, bundle packages
Negotiate P&T contract to capture some cost savings
Monitor AGT winner's market performance over the next contract year before reconsidering switch
